about: Cylindrical steel pins, dowels and ground rods by diameter d, mm, with the lengths a project stocks. DIN 6325 / ISO 8734 (hardened, ground, tolerance m6) and ISO 2338 (unhardened, m6 or h8). A pin of the nominal bore size is m6: it is up to 0.012 OVER its nominal diameter, so it does not enter a bearing bore or a printed hole of the same nominal size (bearings.shaft_sleeve). "lengths" is the standard series of the diameter as most suppliers stock it; a project lists its own stock in gate/owner/tables.json ("pins": {"sizes": {"5": {"lengths": [...]}}}). A pin is known by a bought or hardware body on the axis of a hole whose own name matches fits.pin_ref_pattern; its diameter and length come from that name ("D5", "5 x 20", "4m6x32"), else its diameter is the row whose press, slip or running fit the hole has.
passage_about: decided: a hole this much or more over the pin is a passage the pin goes through with room, not a fit that holds it; it is asked as a hole of no table
source: Diameters and length series of DIN 6325 / ISO 8734 and ISO 2338 as suppliers list them, written down from reference knowledge of the standards; no row was measured. Check the sheet of the pin you buy, and list your own stock in gate/owner/tables.json.
